stories.headline: Saffron stage, caste clout: Inside Kunda’s Rajput power play
stories.deck: At the high-voltage Ram Katha, Raghuraj Pratap Singh sought to showcase Rajput clout within a broader majoritarian narrative ahead of assembly polls
stories.bodyText:
As the winds of the Assembly elections begin to stir across Uttar Pradesh, the saffron canopies of religious kathas are increasingly doubling as stages for political mobilisation and messaging. This alchemy was on display in Kunda, Pratapgarh, recently, where popular preacher Dhirendra Shastri’s Ram Katha became a theatre of Kshatriya-Thakur assertion, draped in the semantics of Hindutva.
In the run-up to the Katha and at the event, the host, Rajput strongman and MLA Raghuraj Pratap Singh (Raja Bhaiya), championed inclusive Hindutva slogans such as “Hum Sab Hindu Bhai-Bhai,” urging Islam-like unity beyond caste lines, and demanding Indian citizenship for Pakistani Hindu refugees. While the Jansatta Dal (Loktantrik) president called the timing coincidental, political observers note that the gathering largely served as a cross-party consolidation of influential Thakur leaders. Prominent Rajput strongmen and leaders, including Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, Dhananjay Singh, Brijesh Singh, Dinesh Pratap Singh, Mayankeshwar Sharan Singh and rebel SP MLAs Rakesh Pratap Singh and Abhay Singh shared the stage, projecting unified caste strength ahead of elections.

stories.headline: North Korea declares a Swiss diplomat persona non grata and orders him to leave
stories.deck: Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un,c ondemned Switzerland for imposing sanctions on a youth camp in eastern North Korea over its alleged role in the transfer of children from Russia-occupied areas of Ukraine
stories.bodyText:
North Korea on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) declared a senior Swiss diplomat heading the country's newly opened diplomatic office in Pyongyang persona non grata and ordered him to leave the country within 48 hours.
The move came a day after Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, threatened to close the office. She condemned Switzerland for imposing sanctions on a youth camp in eastern North Korea over its alleged role in the transfer of children from Russia-occupied areas of Ukraine.
The Korean Central News Agency said a senior Foreign Ministry official summoned Astier Sylvain, who heads the Swiss diplomatic office that opened in Pyongyang last month, and handed him a notice demanding the office's closure and his departure, in protest of the Swiss sanctions on the Songdowon International Children's Camp in Wonsan.

stories.headline: BSE Sensex jumps over 1,700 points; Nifty50 tops 25,850; top reasons behind rally
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Indian benchmark indices rallied sharply on Wednesday, with the 
BSE Sensex
 jumping over 1,900 points and the Nifty50 climbing above 25,900 in early trade.
Strong foreign fund inflows, easing crude oil prices, buying in heavyweight banking stocks and resilient corporate earnings supported the rally, even as global markets remained volatile amid concerns over AI-linked stocks.
The BSE Sensex surged 1,969.80 points, or 2.39%, to 84,405.79, while the 
Nifty 50
 jumped 573.90 points, or 2.26%, to 25,923.55 at 11:10 am.
Earlier, the 30-share Sensex jumped 1,382.16 points to 83,818.15, while the 50-share Nifty advanced 407.60 points to 25,758.45 in the opening session.
The rally followed Monday's sharp selloff, when the Sensex plunged 1,483.72 points, or 1.77%, to close at 82,435.99, while the Nifty fell 450.95 points, or 1.75%, to 25,349.65. Stock markets were closed on Tuesday on account of Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev.
Top 5 reasons behind the stock market rally1. Strong foreign fund inflows
Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) continued to buy Indian equities, providing strong support to domestic markets. Foreign investors purchased shares worth Rs 5,672.99 crore on Monday, according to exchange data.
Foreign inflows into India have strengthened this month, reflecting a reversal in investor sentiment towards domestic equities.
V K Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments, said, "The total reversal of the FII stance towards India is reflected in the FII investment into India, so far, this month at a record $13.2 billion."
2. Lower crude oil prices
Crude oil prices eased on Wednesday, helping improve India's macroeconomic outlook and reducing concerns over inflation and the country's import bill.
Brent crude futures fell 0.5% to $90.97 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) declined 0.6% to $81.58 a barrel. Both benchmarks had gained more than 2% on Tuesday.
Prices have been under pressure amid rising supply and expectations of a market surplus, despite concerns over supply disruptions in the Middle East.
3. Rupee rises 23 paise against US dollar
Rupee strengthened 23 paise to 92.62 against the US dollar in early trade on Wednesday, supported by foreign fund inflows, strong domestic equities and lower crude oil prices.
The rupee opened at 92.65 in the interbank foreign exchange market and subsequently gained to 92.62 against the greenback.
A stronger US dollar, however, capped gains in the domestic currency. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of six currencies, rose 0.15% to 103.90.
Earlier on Monday, rupee had declined 23 paise to close at 92.85 against the dollar, retreating from its seven-month high.
4. Heavyweight banking stocks lead gains
Banking stocks were among the biggest contributors to the market rally, with strong buying in heavyweight private lenders lifting benchmark indices.
HDFC Bank surged 3.54%, Infosys gained 3.43%, ICICI Bank rose 3.19%, Bajaj Finance advanced 2.65%, Axis Bank added 2.13% and Bajaj Finserv climbed 2.09%.
The Nifty Private Bank index gained 2.27%, while the Nifty PSU Bank index rose 0.68%.
Financial stocks gained 2.2% in broader sectoral trade, with HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Reliance Industries also among the major contributors to the rally.
5. Strong corporate earnings support sentiment
Domestic earnings have provided support to Indian equities despite volatility in global markets.
Vijayakumar said, "It is important to understand that India’s improving fundamentals, as reflected in the impressive 27% earnings growth of Nifty 50 in Q2 has the potential to support the increasing FII inflows and impart resilience to the market."
Investors have also been shifting funds towards Indian equities as global markets face uncertainty over valuations and spending in the artificial intelligence sector.
"Earnings have provided a domestic anchor, while rotation away from Asian AI trades have also helped redirect capital towards India," Venkatesh Balasubramaniam and Shanay Mehta of JM Financial told Reuters.
A sharp correction in crude prices has also reduced pressure on the macroeconomic outlook, the analyst added.
6. Recovery after Monday's selloff; global AI trade volatility
Indian markets rebounded after Monday's sharp correction, with investors looking to recover losses amid heightened volatility in global equities.
Vijayakumar said global markets have been witnessing sharp swings driven by AI-linked stocks, with movements in the Nasdaq influencing technology-heavy markets across Asia, including South Korea, Taiwan and Japan.
"There is heightened volatility in global equity markets caused mainly by the swings in AI trade. When the Nasdaq goes down other AI markets like South Korea, Taiwan and Japan, too, go down; when Nasdaq bounces back, these AI trade-dominated markets, too, bounce back. The derivatives trade is aggravating the down moves and up moves in the market, as happened in India last Monday," he said.
"Investors should ignore these wild moves and noise associated with this hyper speculative trade and focus on the fundamentals. From the fundamentals perspective, the Indian market looks resilient," he added.
The rally extended beyond frontline stocks, with broader markets opening in positive territory. The Nifty 100 rose 1.38%, while the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 gained 0.89% and 0.48%, respectively.
Among sectoral indices, the Nifty IT jumped 2.39%, the Nifty Private Bank advanced 2.27%, the Nifty FMCG gained 0.96% and the Nifty Pharma rose 0.98%. The Nifty Auto edged up 0.19%.
However, Tata Steel, Mahindra & Mahindra, Titan and Power Grid were among the stocks trading lower.
The rally in Indian equities came despite weakness across several major Asian markets, where technology stocks faced renewed selling amid global AI-related volatility and concerns over fresh US tariffs.
South Korea's Kospi fell 5.30%, Japan's Nikkei 225 declined 2.74% and Shanghai's SSE Composite index dropped 1%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng traded marginally higher.
The US markets also ended mixed on Tuesday. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48% and the S&P 500 declined 0.50%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.85%.

stories.headline: Shivakumar meets Japan Minister Nakasone in Tokyo, stresses stronger economic ties
stories.bodyText:
Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar during a meeting with Japan State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Yasutaka Nakasone, in Tokyo, Japan.
Credit: @CMofKarnataka/X via PTI Photo
Bengaluru: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Wednesday met Japan's State Minister for Foreign Affairs Yasutaka Nakasone in Tokyo and emphasised the need to strengthen economic cooperation and bilateral collaboration between Japan and Karnataka, officials said.
During the meeting, Shivakumar encouraged greater Japanese investment in Karnataka, they said.
He invited a high-level Japanese government delegation to participate in Karnataka's Global Investors Meet 2027, along with a dedicated Japan Country Pavilion, the Chief Minister's office said in a statement.
Shivakumar also expressed his gratitude for Japan's continued support for key infrastructure projects, including the Bengaluru Metro and Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board, and sought further collaboration on Karnataka's developmental priorities, it said.
Japan's State Minister for Foreign Affairs welcomed the delegation led by the chief minister and appreciated the strong and enduring India-Japan relationship, it said.
Nakasone also underscored Karnataka's importance as a key destination for Japanese investments and welcomed continued engagement between Japan and Karnataka.

briefs.headline: India warns against using tech for strategic one-upmanship, calls for inclusive AI governance
briefs.deck: India’s UN Ambassador asserted that amid the rapid integration of AI into military and intelligence spheres, responsibility for the use of lethal autonomous weapons systems must always rest with humans
briefs.bodyText:
India has voiced concern over the instrumentalisation of technology for strategic one-upmanship through export control and licensing regimes, calling out the tendency to treat countries of the Global South as mere consumers as it underscored that technological transformation must not deepen existing inequalities.
Addressing the Security Council’s high-level open debate on Maintenance of International Peace and Security on ‘Conflict Resolution in an Era of Rapid Technological Change’, India’s Permanent Representative to the UN Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni said AI systems can inadvertently perpetuate biases related to gender, language and socio-economic background.
“We note with concern the emerging medium- and long-term trends of technology denial and the instrumentalisation of technology for strategic one-upmanship through export control and licensing regimes, and a tendency to treat countries of the Global South as mere consumers without any agency or stake in how emerging technologies such as AI are developed, are regulated and are deployed,” Mr. Parvathaneni said.
“AI must not reduce human beings to mere data points or raw material. India supports inclusive international cooperation on technology governance, including through the United Nations, with due regard to national priorities and developmental needs,” he said.
He emphasised that technology should serve humanity, strengthen international cooperation, and advance the cause of lasting peace.
“Technology may inform human judgement but cannot and should not replace it,” he said.
India also asserted that amid the rapid integration of artificial intelligence into military and intelligence spheres, responsibility for use of lethal autonomous weapons systems must always rest with humans.
“Rapid technological advances are fundamentally transforming the nature of conflict and the international security landscape. Artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and emerging digital technologies present unprecedented opportunities but also introduce new vulnerabilities and risks across the entire conflict cycle,” Mr. Parvathaneni said.
He added that the rapid integration of artificial intelligence into military, intelligence, and civilian spheres has fundamentally transformed the landscape of international peace and security.
India stressed that the application of emerging technologies in conflict settings must be responsible, human-centric, respect sovereignty, and adhere to international law.
“Emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapons systems raise legitimate legal and ethical questions. India is committed to addressing these within the framework of the Convention on Prohibitions or Restrictions on the Use of Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW), which seeks to balance military necessity with humanitarian considerations,” Mr. Parvathaneni said.
He underscored that human judgement and oversight remain essential, taking into account the operational context and characteristics of the weapons system. “Responsibility for the use of such systems must always rest with humans,” the Indian envoy said, adding that leveraging technology for protection must be a cross-cutting and cross-sectoral measure.
“It must be used for the protection of civilians and of peacekeepers and should be leveraged for the protection of humanitarian personnel.”
India called on the international community to address threats posed by misuse of emerging technologies such as AI.
“The risks associated with AI are real, and we must address them without any hesitation. The potential misuse of these emerging technologies by terrorists and non-State actors is a matter of grave concern. Incomplete, inaccurate, or deliberately manipulated data through AI can undermine decision-making,” he said.
He told the Council that India has made robust advancements in digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, and emerging technologies, reflecting a clear emphasis on protecting critical information infrastructure and ensuring the continuity of essential civilian services.
Addressing the Security Council Open Debate, Secretary General Antonio Guterres voiced concern that today’s wars have become “proving grounds” for AI-enabled targeting.
Asserting that killer robots must have no place in the world’s future, Mr. Guterres reiterated his call to urgently launch negotiations for a legally binding instrument on lethal autonomous weapons systems.
“AI is driving greater autonomy across military functions. From intelligence gathering to target selection, it is reported that algorithms are increasingly shaping life-and-death decisions,” he said, adding that these capabilities are within the reach of both States and non-State armed groups.
“And the potential integration of AI with nuclear command, control and communication systems is a recipe for catastrophe. As long as nuclear weapons exist, the decision to use them must rest with human beings alone,” Mr. Guterres said.
“When civilians are killed, or human rights are violated, the answer must never be ‘the algorithm did it’,” Mr. Guterres said.
The UN chief added that humans must always retain control over life-and-death decisions – guided by international law and ethical principles.
“Technology companies must reckon with the legal risks they may face if their services contribute to violations of international law. And no country should design, develop, deploy, or use military applications of AI in armed conflict that violate international law, international humanitarian law, or international human rights law,” he said.

briefs.headline: Tamil Nadu government set to ink 70 MoUs for investments to the tune of over ₹50,000 crore
briefs.deck: Sources said the MoUs would cover sectors including manufacturing, clean energy, textiles, aerospace and defence
briefs.bodyText:
Tamil Nadu is set to sign over 70 memoranda of understanding (MoUs), entailing investments of over Rs. 50,000 crore, at the VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave, scheduled to be held in Chennai on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).
Sources said the MoUs would cover sectors including manufacturing, clean energy, textiles, aerospace and defence.
It is learnt that Royal Enfield will be signing a deal for EV motorbikes.
Keppel-backed Cleantech Solar, a renewable energy developer with a portfolio of 1.2 MWp+ renewable energy projects, including over 400 MW in Tamil Nadu, is also signing a deal. This will be a five-year investment, integrating solar, wind and battery energy storage systems, designed to meet the evolving energy requirements of Tamil Nadu’s commercial and industrial sectors.
Sources say the two South Korean automotive component manufacturers — Seoyon E-Hwa Summit Automotive India Private Limited and Hwashin Automotive India Private Limited — that recently expressed interest in investing in Tamil Nadu will also be signing MoUs.
“Turning investment intent into working facilities and steady livelihoods is what matters most for our people. Our focus is on practical execution, responsive institutions, and balanced industrial growth across Tamil Nadu,” Industries Minister S. Keerthana said.
Status report
The TVK government will also provide an update on the MoUs signed since the party came to power, including the number of project proposals that have translated into actual investments. It will also present a status report on the remaining projects, detailing their progress at various stages, such as land acquisition and construction.
At its first investors’ conclave held in August this year, the TVK government signed 97 MoUs, entailing more than Rs. 67,542 crore in investments.

briefs.headline: China to launch Shenzhou-20 spaceflight on April 24
briefs.deck: The Shenzhou-20 spaceflight will carry three astronauts namely Chen Dong, Chen Zhongrui and Wang Jie
briefs.bodyText:
China has set the launch for its Shenzhou-20 mission that will carry three astronauts to the Chinese space station for Thursday (April 24, 2025) at 5.17 p.m. local time (IST 2:47 p.m.), state media said on Wednesday (April 23, 2025).
The main purpose of the mission is to complete the in-orbit rotation with the Shenzhou-19 crew which is scheduled to return to the Dongfeng landing site on April 29, officials said at a press conference broadcast on CCTV.
The Shenzhou-20 spaceflight will carry astronauts Chen Dong, Chen Zhongrui and Wang Jie, CCTV said.
They will conduct space science and application experiments, install a space debris protection device as well as extravehicular payload and equipment, and perform recovery tasks.
The mission will also bring with it zebrafish, planarians and streptomyces as research objects to carry out three life science experiments at the space station.

briefs.headline: Delhi wakes up to coldest morning of the season; Air quality ‘poor’
briefs.deck: Air quality in Delhi remained in the ‘poor’ category, with four monitoring stations recording 'very poor' readings, even as the city's average AQI stood at 224
briefs.bodyText:
Delhi recorded its coldest morning of the season on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), with the minimum temperature settling at 10°C.
The minimum temperature at Safdarjung, the city's base weather station, was 1.3° below the season's normal, while it dropped by 1.2° degrees compared to the previous day.
Air quality in Delhi remained in the ‘poor’ category, with four monitoring stations recording 'very poor' readings, even as the city's average Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 224.
The total number of weather stations active at 9:05 a.m. was 56 out of the total 59 in the city.
Other parts of the city also recorded relatively low temperatures. Lodhi Road recorded a minimum of 10.1°C, followed by Ayanagar at 10.4° , Palam at 11° and the Ridge at 11.7°.
The minimum temperature at Palam remained unchanged from Tuesday (November 24), while Lodhi Road recorded a drop of 0.6°. The Ridge saw a fall of 0.3° degrees, while Ayanagar recorded a marginal rise of 0.2°.
No rainfall was recorded at any of the five weather stations during the 24 hours ending at 8:30 a.m. on Wednesday (November 25).
According to the CPCB, an AQI between 0 and 50 is classified as 'good', 51 and 100 as 'satisfactory', 101 and 200 as 'moderate', 201 and 300 as 'poor', 301 and 400 as 'very poor', and 401 and 500 as 'severe'.
The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecasted shallow fog for the day, and the maximum temperature is likely to touch 25°C.

briefs.headline: Government examining measures to curb human-elephant conflict in Hassan, says Forest Minister
briefs.deck: Ramalinga Reddy says steel-rope barriers and GPS collars are among options to address the issue
briefs.bodyText:
The State government is examining a series of measures to address the growing problem of human-elephant conflict in Hassan district, including the installation of steel-rope barricades and fitting GPS collars on elephants to monitor their movements, Minister for Forest, Ecology and Environment Ramalinga Reddy said on Tuesday.
The Minister said residents of Belur, Sakleshpur and other parts of Hassan district have been facing difficulties owing to elephant movement, and the State government was taking their concerns seriously.
The Minister was speaking to presspersons after inaugurating the new main entrance gate and various development works at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Zoological Park at Kamalapura near Hampi in Vijayanagara district. The works were taken up at a cost of ₹18 crore with assistance from the Vijayanagara District Mineral Foundation and other sources. He also laid the foundation stone for additional works estimated to cost ₹3 crore.
Pointing to the fragmented nature of forest areas in the region, he said nearly 13,000 acres of forest in Belur taluk were spread across nine separate patches, and the nearly one lakh acres of forest area in Sakleshpur were similarly divided into more than 80 patches. “This fragmentation made it difficult to regulate elephant movement and prevent human-elephant conflict,” he said.
The proposal to relocate elephants to the Bhadra forest area had been under discussion for some time, and the government would also take into consideration the concerns expressed by local elected representatives, Mr. Reddy said.
“The feasibility of installing steel-rope barricades to prevent elephants from straying out of forests is being examined, subject to financial constraints. A plan to fit GPS collars on elephants and continuously monitor their movements was also being implemented,” he said.
Kamalapur zoo development
Speaking on the development initiatives taken at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Zoological Park at Kamalapura near Hampi in Vijayanagara district, Mr. Reddy said that several facilities have been developed at the zoo with funding from the Vijayanagara District Mineral Foundation, the Karnataka Mining Environment Restoration Corporation and contributions from mining companies.
“Hampi is an important historical destination that attracts a large number of tourists. The government is committed to developing the zoo as an additional attraction,” he said.
The Minister said that arrangements had been made to ensure an uninterrupted supply of water, fodder and food for the animals and birds. Solar-powered borewells had been installed to ensure a regular water supply and to meet emergency requirements. Shade had also been provided for the animals, while a sprinkler system had been introduced to maintain the plants.
The zoo would be provided with additional animal species, with priority given to their health and conservation, he said. New open and closed jeeps and buses had also been arranged to facilitate safari tours.

briefs.headline: 'My face is not an Instagram filter': Jasmin Bhasin reacts to plastic surgery rumours, says she's 'allowed to look different'
briefs.bodyText:
Television actor Jasmin Bhasin on November 24 slammed rumours of plastic surgery after her new pictures left netizens pointing out that she "looks different", fuelling rumours of Botox, fillers and cosmetic surgery.
The conversation started when the Bigg Boss Season 14 contestant uploaded a carousel of images from a wedding she attended in Kolkata.
In the pictures, the 36-year-old actor was seen dressed in a pink lehenga with statement jewellery. Actor Aly Goni, comedian Munawar Faruqui and YouTuber Elvish Yadav were also seen in the photos.
It wasn't long after Bhasin shared the photos that the netizens started pointing out she "looks different", and soon rumours of a plastic surgery were rife.
Dismissing the rumours of a plastic surgery, Bhasin took to her Instagram Story and responded to the allegations, stressing that she is made of "blood, flesh, muscles and bones" and is "allowed to look different."
"So apparently I've had a new plastic surgery every time I've had a slightly different face," she wrote.
She continued, "Guys, relax. I travel, I don't sleep enough, I work with different make-up artists, my sinus gets inflamed, I get exhausted, I've started strength training, I've gained some weight."
Screengrab of Jasmin Bhasin's Instagram Story.
"My face is not a permanent Instagram filter," she wrote, while adding, "Some days the face is snatched. Some days the face is swollen. Some days the face is tired. Some days even the makeup is fighting for its life."
Taking a sarcastic jibe at the plastic surgery rumours, Bhasin added that she doesn't even have time for it.
"And the “plastic surgery” theories... yaaar, plastic surgery karwane ke liye bhi toh time chahiye! I'm literally made of blood, flesh, muscles and bones. I'm allowed to look different on different days," she continued.
Urging people to stop the intense scrutiny of her pictures, she concluded, "And honestly? I love my face. I love my body. I love myself. I don't need to look perfect every day to be happy with how I look. So please... let this human breathe."
Bhasin is known for her stint in Bigg Boss Season 14 and Khatron Ke Khiladi 15. She was last seen in the Punjabi film Judaa.
She rose to fame with the romantic drama television series Tashan-e-Ishq where she played Twinkle Taneja.

stories.headline: Bengaluru woman’s Rs 12.7 lakh Groww portfolio falls to Rs 84,508 after tech glitch during Rs 10 lakh withdrawal; firm told to refund Rs 11.85 lakh with 6% interest and pay Rs 12,000
stories.deck: Ranjana Priya's investment of Rs 8.12 lakhs in the Groww app initially flourished, reaching Rs 12.7 lakhs. However, upon seeking a redemption of Rs 10 lakhs, she was shocked to see her portfolio plummet to just Rs 84,508. After numerous complaints went unanswered, the Bengaluru Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission deemed Groww liable for unfair practices, ultimately ordering them to refund Rs…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Imagine watching your savings grow to over Rs 12 lakh on an investment app, only to see the balance shrink to under Rs 1 lakh the moment you try to withdraw your own money. That is what a city woman faced when the Groww app displayed a sudden, unexplained error after she sought a redemption. The Bengaluru (Urban) District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has held the platform liable for deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.
The saga began when Ranjana Priya, a resident of HSR Layout, Sector 2, trusted the platform's market reputation and assurances and invested a total of Rs 8.12 lakhs through systematic investment plans (SIPs) on the Groww app. Favourable market performance pushed her portfolio up significantly, and the official dashboard showed its valuation had reached Rs 12,70,404 as of November 26, 2025.
Citing urgent personal and financial requirements, she placed a digital request for a partial redemption of Rs 10 lakh. What followed, she said, were "alarming errors". The dashboard updated to show her total invested amount as just Rs 84,508, wiping out the rest of her portfolio value.
Priya said she ran from pillar to post, raising support tickets by phone and email and complaining to SEBI on November 27. Nothing was resolved. 
On November 30, Groww credited a mere Rs 15,500 to her bank account. By her reconciliation, her total investment value stood at Rs 12.70 lakhs. After accounting for the amount redeemed, Rs 11.85 lakhs was left unaccounted for.
She then raised statutory grievances on the e-Jagriti platform through WhatsApp four times between December 7 and December 25, 2025. The opposite parties neither corrected their financial records nor refunded the balance. Leaving her with no option, Priya approached the commission on April 22, 2026, and sought a refund for mental agony, harassment and financial hardship.
She named Groww Invest Tech Pvt Ltd and Nextbillion Technology Pvt Ltd (Groww)/Billionbrains Garage Ventures Pvt Ltd. Both appeared through counsel but did not file their written version within the statutory 45 days. Their version was taken as not filed, in line with a judgment of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, and despite sufficient opportunities, they never mounted a defence.
After going through the records and hearing arguments, the commission observed that her allegations stood unchallenged as the firms had forfeited their right to defence. It accepted as true her digital records, including the portfolio value of Rs 12.7 lakhs and the redemption request for Rs 10 lakh. The platform's act of reducing the visible portfolio value to Rs 84,508, coupled with its complete failure to respond to four separate institutional warnings from the National Grievance Helpline, amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice, it said. It termed the withholding of Rs 11.85 lakhs belonging to a retail investor "completely unauthorised, illegal and high handed".
The commission added that a digital investment platform cannot hold a consumer's hard-earned savings hostage under the guise of an unrectified technical glitch or internal database error. The documents showed beyond doubt that of her Rs 12. 7 lakhs portfolio, Rs 11.85 lakhs remained unaccounted for and was withheld without valid legal justification, causing mental agony and financial distress to a complainant dependent on her savings.
The commission, comprising president Ramachandra MS and members Nandini H Kumbhar and Savitha Airani directed both firms, jointly and severally, to refund Rs 11,85,896 with 6% annual interest from the date of redemption until actual realisation. It further ordered them to pay Rs 10,000 for deficiency in service and mental harassment and Rs 2,000 as litigation costs.

stories.headline: Karnataka hikes women's reservation to 50% for long-delayed rural poll
stories.deck: Karnataka is preparing for long-overdue rural elections by announcing new reservations for panchayat seats. The government has increased women's representation from 33% to 50%, benefiting more candidates. Rural development minister Eshwar Khandre mentioned that elections might occur in January next year. However, progress is dependent on final electoral rolls from the Election Commission. The…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Karnataka moved towards holding long-delayed rural elections Tuesday, announcing reservations for 4,681 zilla and taluk panchayat seats and raising women's quota from 33% to 50%. Elections to 30 zilla panchayats and 234 taluk panchayats have not been held since their terms ended in 2021.
Rural development and panchayati raj minister Eshwar Khandre said elections were expected in Jan, but the state election commission (SEC) was yet to receive the final electoral rolls from EC, a delay that could hold up the announcement of the poll schedule. SEC must publish the draft electoral rolls before finalising the voters' list.
The last panchayat elections were held in 2016, leaving rural local bodies without elected representatives for nearly five years.
Khandre said govt had notified reservations for 1,101 zilla panchayat and 3,580 taluk panchayat seats. "With this exercise, state govt's role is complete," he said.
The govt, however, withheld the reservation list for Bengaluru zilla panchayat.
Taking a swipe at the previous BJP govt, Khandre said it had failed to conduct elections until 2023. "When Congress took charge, we took up many pending panchayat upgrades," he said.

stories.headline: Theatre by ZLB 23: Bengaluru’s most intimate cocktail experience
stories.deck: The Leela Palace Bengaluru’s seven-seater bar combines cinematic AI-led storytelling, experimental cocktails and high-tech mixology. But the bartender is the real star of this immersive drinking experience
stories.bodyText:
Captain Nair would have loved The Theatre by ZLB 23. After all, his eyes sparkled with delight at the prospect of drama of any kind. And Theatre, a secretive, 7 seater-space tucked into The Leela Palace Bengaluru’s award winning speakeasy ZLB 23 is all about creating a memorable spectacle.
When I first met the founder of The Leela Palaces, Hotels and Resorts in 2016, at the opening of The Leela Palace Chennai, he was 90, bouncing with delight and trailed by a large entourage of hoteliers. Dapper in the high-waisted white trousers favoured by his generation, his warm tan suit snazzy with a boldly patterned silk tie and pocket square, he insisted on taking me through the twists and turns of every stage of his life, with Spielberg-like attention to detail: How he was stationed in Abbottabad as a wireless officer in 1942, popularised the legendary bleeding Madras fabric in the ‘60s, and then became a hotelier in the 80s, at the age of 65.
Our interview began over coffee and ended at dinner, five hours later.
When I left, he gallantly walked me to my car, still followed by his visibly tiring entourage. He then directed his team to put an entire chocolate cake on the seat beside me, along with a pile of glossy magazines, so I could snack and read on my 20-minute ride home.
The late Captain Nair instinctively understood luxury. It is not just plush carpeting and glittering chandeliers; it is also the promise of escape. It is a glamorous cocoon for people to slip into when they need a break, where comfort is anticipated, and guests are made to genuinely cared for. His legacy lives on in the The Leela Palace Bengaluru’s lush garden, an extravagance of more than 30 varieties of palm trees, wrapped in coils of Monstera, and birdsong, all set in the heart of the city.
Although Brookfield Asset Management bought the hotel chain in 2019, the founder’s flamboyance is all over the 7.5-acre property, inspired by the Mysore Palace with yalis at the entrance, a ceiling covered in 22-carat gold leaf and an uruli belonging to his wife Leela, filled with rose petals at the entrance.
We meander through the garden to get to ZLB 23, the award winning speakeasy, which glitters like a scene from The Great Gatsby with chandeliers dripping crystals, moody lighting and beautiful people.
Its latest secret is a speakeasy within this speakeasy: The Theatre, an intimate space for 7 people. The stage, which is built like a lab, glimmers with high tech bartending equipment, including a Thermomix, a Rotovap and a freeze-drier, and features a large screen as a backdrop. It faces a cosy little living room set up with leather couches set around a low table, bustling with books, Perrier and bowls of salted, butter, cheese, and caramel popcorn.
Manoranjan Moktan aka MJ, bartender and star of The Theatre’s performances, describes it as ‘a bartender’s living room’. There are three shows here a day, at 7 pm, 9 pm and 11 pm, each lasting two hours. During each sitting, MJ or one of his colleagues plays host, narrator and lead performer, making four cocktails while the backstory of each drink unfolds on the screen like a short film.
The menu, Secrets of Taste, opens with an aperitivo built with Japanese whisky, makrut lime, and vermouth, laced with fresh strawberries to soften the edges. When the curtains go up, the movie and cocktail take shape together. It is a unique idea, building anticipation around each drink. But, the AI-generated films, like most AI generated content like now, are predictably vapid, pivoting on formulaic storytelling and generic scripts. As it turns out, the highlight of Theatre is not the theatre, but the team behind the bar.
At every break between the reels, I sit on a barstool and MJ patiently explains how each drink comes together, pulling out dark corked bottles of distillates and jars of preserves to illustrate his points. I try the punchy coriander concentrate he uses in his cocktails, and take deep appreciative sniffs of his bowl of pink rosebuds gathered from the Valley of Flowers.
The drinks are intricate, smooth and designed like art: especially their deliciously boozy spin on the Margarita, featuring four layers of citrus – grapefruit, yuzu, orange and lime – and frozen peels coiled together instead of conventional ice. As I sip on each cocktail, we swap stories, and MJ, who confesses he has a weakness for espresso martinis, tells me about his hometown in Nepal, near the border with Darjeeling. We end the night at ZLB23, where the bartenders introduce us to a chilled and satisfyingly savoury rasam-inspired cocktail stiff with tequila, sweet with pineapple and served with a curry leaf rim.
The Theatre is designed to be a luxury night out that merges cinema and cocktails. It is an ambitious idea, powered by elaborate equipment and smooth pours. But it’s greatest strength is the team, who are enthusiastic about their craft and genuinely excited to share their knowledge. AI, no matter how slick, will never compare.
As Captain Nair understood, long before hospitality became an industry obsessed with Insta-friendly displays, luxury is really about people, and paying attention.
Open Monday to Saturday (7 PM, 9 PM, and 11 PM). At Leela Palace Bengaluru, Old Airport Road

stories.headline: Gold, silver price fall boosts retail sales but raises concerns among jewellers in Bengaluru
stories.deck: While jewellers have reported an increase in sales following the decline in prices, industry representatives remain divided over its impact on businesses and the future movement of prices.
stories.bodyText:
The sharp decline in gold and silver prices over the past 15 days has brought relief to jewellery buyers, particularly those planning weddings and purchasing precious metals for gifting, even as it has raised concerns among investors and traders over potential losses.
While jewellers have reported an increase in sales following the decline in prices, industry representatives remain divided over its impact on businesses and the future movement of prices.
According to market rates on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), 24-carat gold was priced at ₹12,780 per gram, down from around ₹18,000 per gram in January 2026. Prices had remained in the range of ₹15,000 to ₹16,000 per gram during September and October. Silver prices have also witnessed a steep decline, falling from around ₹3.5 lakh and ₹4 lakh per kg to ₹1.6 lakh per kg.
Srinivas R., honorary secretary of the Jewellers Association, Bengaluru, said that the gold prices had declined by around 34%, while silver prices had fallen by nearly 60%, creating both opportunities and challenges for different sections of the market.
“The current situation can be analysed in two ways. It is a good time for those who want to purchase gold and silver for weddings or gift them to their loved ones. However, it is definitely not a good time for investors who purchased precious metals earlier, expecting good returns or profits from selling them. They may have to wait for the next two months. As per my prediction, gold prices could decline further to around ₹11,500 per gram,” he said.
T.A. Sharavana, founder and owner of Shree Sai Gold Palace, said that jewellery shops have witnessed an increase in sales over the past 15 days as customers sought to take advantage of the lower prices.
“This is the first time in history that gold prices have risen to ₹18,000 per gram and subsequently fallen to around ₹12,000 within just 10 months. A similar trend has been witnessed in silver prices,” he said.
However, he pointed out that the price correction could adversely affect newly established jewellery businesses, particularly those that had borrowed money from banks and private financiers to set up their shops and purchase inventory.
“Established businesses that have been operating for several years may be able to absorb or compensate for the losses. However, newly opened shops could face difficulties. According to my calculation, gold and silver businesses could incur losses of around 25%, considering the expenditure on employee salaries, electricity bills and other operational costs,” he added.
Disagreeing with the assessment of losses, B. Ramachary, president of the Karnataka State Jewellers Federation (KSJW), said the decline in prices would not necessarily translate into losses for most jewellery businesses.
He said several jewellers would have purchased gold and silver at lower prices in January and February and sold them to customers when rates were significantly higher, ranging between ₹15,000 and ₹18,000 per gram. The profits earned during that period, he said, could offset any losses arising from the current price correction.
Mr. Ramachary also advised those planning to invest in gold and silver to wait until December 9, when the U.S. Federal Reserve is scheduled to review its interest rates.
“Depending on whether interest rates are increased or reduced, investment patterns in gold and silver could change. This could influence demand and prices. With changes in demand and supply, prices are expected to rise by the middle of December,” he said.
No major impact on gold loans
Meanwhile, the decline in gold prices is unlikely to have a significant impact on existing gold loan borrowers, said Gopal Krishnan, former president and head of the law department at Axis Bank.
He said fluctuations in gold prices were a regular feature of the market and banks generally accounted for such movements while extending loans against pledged jewellery.
“There will not be a huge impact on gold loans as gold prices keep fluctuating. Banks or private financiers may ask borrowers to clear the outstanding balance or pledge additional gold if the value of the collateral falls significantly. However, banks have not issued any such notices to customers even during previous periods of price decline,” he said.
What influences gold and silver prices?
Several global factors influence the prices of precious metals, including geopolitical tensions, inflation, government debt levels and interest rates.
Mr. Srinivas said governments facing financial pressures could sell portions of their gold reserves to raise funds, potentially increasing supply in the market and exerting downward pressure on prices.
“Rising interest rates in the U.S. could also make interest-bearing bank deposits and other financial instruments more attractive to investors than gold and silver, which do not generate regular returns,” he added.
Silver prices, meanwhile, are influenced not only by investment demand but also by industrial consumption, according to Mr. Srinivas. “Demand from sectors such as solar energy, electric vehicles and data centres plays an important role in determining prices. Efforts by industries to explore alternative materials to silver could also influence its future demand and price movements,” he said.

briefs.headline: Jammers, scanners & five-layer locks: Inside Karnataka Examinations Authority’s machinery
briefs.bodyText:
Once called the Common Entrance Test Cell (CET-Cell), the present Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA) was established in 1994 to conduct entrance tests and determine the eligibility for admission to the govt share of seats in professional courses.
KEA has evolved over time. Today, it is a recruiting agency for civil services with powers on a par with Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC). But what makes it stand apart is that it is bereft of any controversy. KEA holds 56 recruiting exams ranging from the police department to handlooms and textiles department, apart from the college/school admissions entrance tests. Last week, H Prasanna, executive director of KEA, made a presentation to the Centre’s High-Powered Task Force (HPTF) on exam reforms, headed by 
Nandan Nilekani
, on how it conducts exams.
How Question Bank is CreatedStage 1
* The complete question paper will not be prepared by any single resource person or group of resource persons
* Subject experts will be invited to prepare questions on a chapter-wise basis
* Exam-related details will not be disclosed to resource persons
* 50–60% of resource persons will be from Karnataka
* Karnataka-based resource persons must prepare questions in both Kannada and English. Resource persons from outside Karnataka will prepare questions in English. Translation support will be provided separately
* Questions will be organised subject-wise and chapter-wise
* A sufficiently large question bank will be maintained, normally in the ratio of 1:10 to 1:20 against the required questions
Stage 2
* Senior subject experts will be invited for independent scrutiny of questions
* Questions will undergo detailed review for: accuracy of translation, subject knowledge and technical correctness, correctness of answer key, quality of question framing, ambiguity, duplication and other errors
Preparation of Question Paper
* Controller of examinations (CoE) will personally select the required questions from approved question bank
* Normally, 100 questions will be selected for each question paper
* Selected question scripts will be handed over directly to the authorised printing agency
* The selection and handover process will generally take place 15–30 days before exam, depending on the number of candidates
* The printing agency will only digitise the selected questions and undertake proof checking
* Any clarification required by the printer will be obtained through a strictly confidential process
* Questions will be digitised and categorised subject-wise and chapter-wise
* Each question will be classified into three difficulty levels: easy, moderate, difficult
* CoE will determine the total number of questions as well as chapter-wise, subject-wise, and difficulty-level distribution
* The software will randomly select and arrange questions based on the predefined parameters. The final question paper will be generated automatically through the software
* CoE will hand over the final soft copy through a secure pen drive to the authorised printer. Since proofreading is completed during digitisation and question selection is automated from the approved database, separate proofreading at the printing stage will not normally be required
Printing
* Question papers are printed outside Karnataka at high-security printing presses
* Strict confidentiality and security protocols are followed throughout the printing process and transportation
Transportation
* Printed question papers are packed using a minimum of five layers of tamper-proof security packaging
* Packets are transported in one-time lockable security trunks, ensuring that any unauthorised access is detectable
Security features
* Facial recognition technology: scanner-integrated devices, real-time attendance, using diploma students as volunteers
* Airport-style frisking
* Police inspector / sub-inspector will be supervising frisking
* Police constables or home guards are deployed
* Live monitoring of all exam centres at deputy commissioner’s office and the exam centre
* Live CCTV monitoring
* Command room surveillance
* 24 candidates per room
* Installation of mobile signal jammers to prevent candidates or others from capturing and transmitting question papers through mobile phones during the exam
* To prevent classroom copying: 12 different series of question papers used with randomised question order. 
Answer options will also be shuffled, making copying between candidates extremely difficult.
* Two Invigilators per exam room
* 5th circle shading: mandatory for unanswered questions. Prevents post-exam tampering. ¼ mark deduction if not shaded
* KEA publishes the answered OMR sheets on its website on the same day as exam to prevent manipulation
* Triple copies of OMR: one for candidate, one for KEA scanning and evaluation, one for secure custody with the DC/in KEA’s designated strongroom
What Next?
KEA can transition to Computer-Based Testing (CBT) in a phased manner. The technical education department may be involved in this initiative, as it has the required exam infrastructure and technical human resources to support the transition.
Single exam for recruitment to various posts, including first division assistant, second division assistant and other equivalent posts across different departments that need similar educational qualifications.

briefs.headline: Nandan Nilekani-led task force reviews Karnataka exams model as KEA showcases anti-malpractice measures
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: At a time when question paper leaks, irregularities and malpractices have raised serious questions about the credibility of competitive examinations, Karnataka’s model of conducting exams has caught the attention of the central task force headed by 
Nandan Nilekani
.
The high-powered taskforce on public examinations reforms recently held a consultation meeting in the state to understand how the Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA) conducts examinations with an emphasis on transparency, accountability and preventing malpractice. The meeting was attended by chief minister 
D K Shivakumar
, officials from the higher education department and KEA representatives.
KEA executive director H Prasanna made a presentation on exam practices, several of which are learnt to have impressed the committee. These include making scanned OMR answer sheets publicly accessible on its website the day of the exam to reduce the scope for post-exam manipulation.
Another initiative that found favour with the task force was the use of CCTV cameras rented by colleges hosting exams. At a nominal cost of Rs 6 per candidate, the arrangement allows KEA to strengthen surveillance without requiring institutions to invest heavily in camera infrastructure. Other security measures at exam centres include facial recognition technology for candidate verification, airport-style frisking and mobile signal jammers.
KEA also suggested a phase-wise shift to computer-based tests.

briefs.headline: PWD floats tenders for 9 Udupi bridges
briefs.bodyText:
Udupi: Food, civil supplies and consumer affairs minister and district minister Rizwan Arshad on Tuesday said the Public Works Department had invited tenders to construct nine bridges in Udupi district. He directed officials to begin work immediately and ensure speedy completion without compromising quality.
Arshad was speaking after laying the foundation stone for the Rs 5-crore Perdoor–Bairampalli–Annalu connecting bridge on Bajagoli–Tenkabettu State Highway. He directed officials to complete the bridge within the stipulated time to facilitate public use.

Satish Jarkiholi
 had helped secure funds for the bridge. He called for its completion before the monsoon and sought state assistance to repair and reconstruct roads damaged by heavy rainfall and local geographical conditions.
At a separate event, Arshad said state govt’s five guarantee schemes were not merely welfare programmes but initiatives intended to transform society. He was speaking after inaugurating a celebration and information workshop for guarantee scheme beneficiaries at Ajjarkadu Mahatma Gandhi district stadium. Arshad said prices of essentials, including food, gas and fuel, were rising nationwide while incomes had not kept pace.
 With millions of young people facing unemployment, govt introduced the schemes to provide direct financial assistance, he said.
Legislative council deputy chairperson Umashree said opposition parties that had criticised Karnataka’s guarantee schemes were implementing similar models in other states. She said benefits were reaching eligible people directly and that payments delayed by technical issues had been cleared. Guarantee schemes implementation committee state president H Revanna, DC Swaroopa TK and Udupi ZP CEO Prateek Bayal attended. briefs.headline: Bomb threat to venue of Diljit Dosanjh’s show in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Security agencies have been placed on high alert ahead of Punjabi singer-actor 
Diljit Dosanjh
’s upcoming concert in the city after authorities received an email threatening an improvised explosive device (IED) blast at the venue. The show, part of Dosanjh’s ongoing ‘Aura’ India tour, is scheduled to be held on Nov 29 at NICE Grounds near the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC) in Madavara under the jurisdiction of Madanayakanahalli police station.
According to police, the threat was initially sent by ‘weismith3727@gmail.com’ to the official email address of the Hubballi-Dharwad municipal corporation commissioner and subsequently shared with the office of the city police commissioner, Bengaluru.
Concluding with the pro-Khalistan slogan “Khalistan Zindabad,” the email warned of an impending IED explosion during the concert. The sender also issued specific warnings to prospective concertgoers, advising them not to bring children to the event, to refrain from picking up or answering unattended iPhones, and to avoid travelling via Metro trains.
Following the alert, police contacted BIEC management, who confirmed that the concert is slated to take place on Nov 29. 
Based on a complaint, cases have been registered under Section 66 of the Information Technology Act, and BNS Sections 351(4) (criminal intimidation) and 353(1)(b) (statements conducing to public mischief).
Cybercrime and technical teams have launched a probe to trace the IP address and establish the origin and authenticity of the email account. Meanwhile, senior police officers stated elaborate security arrangements and anti-sabotage checks are being put in place to ensure a safe event. Organisers have not announced any changes to the concert schedule.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru police probe forgery of six verification certificates, including one for U.S. H-1B visa
briefs.bodyText:
The Bengaluru City Cyber Crime Police have registered an FIR over the alleged fabrication of a fake Police Verification Certificate (PVC) in the name of the Additional Commissioner of Police (Intelligence), Bengaluru, purportedly issued for a U.S. H-1B visa application.
The case was registered on November 16 under Sections 66(C) and 66(D) of the Information Technology Act, 2000, and Sections 318(4), 319(2), 336(2) and 340(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The accused has been booked as an unidentified person.
According to the complaint filed by Nagaraj T. Nedalagi, a police official attached to the Cyber Crime Police Station, the forgery came to light when the office of the Additional Commissioner of Police (Intelligence) received an email seeking verification of the authenticity of a police verification certificate purportedly issued to a person identified as Katla Ramya Sree.
The email, originally sent by Ramya Sree from her Gmail account, was forwarded through the offices of senior police officials and received by the Intelligence wing on October 30. It sought confirmation of a certificate submitted for her U.S. H-1B visa application.
The email contained a PDF copy of the purported certificate bearing the signature of Raman Gupta, Additional Commissioner of Police (Intelligence), Bengaluru City, with reference numbers that were later found to be fake.
However, an examination of the document revealed that it was allegedly fabricated. Police officials clarified that Police Verification Certificates are issued through the Seva Sindhu portal after the verification process is completed, with the digital signatures of the ACP or Police Inspector (Administration).
The department also clarified that the Additional Commissioner of Police (Intelligence) is not the designated authority to sign such certificates. The complaint alleged that unidentified persons had misused the name and designation of the senior police officer to create a forged government document and circulate it as an authentic police verification certificate.
The complainant stated that such fraudulent activity not only causes potential loss to the government exchequer but also undermines public confidence in certificates issued by the police department.
Following instructions from senior officers, the Cyber Crime Police registered a case and initiated an investigation to identify the person responsible for creating and circulating the fake certificate.
In a similar case, the Cyber Crime Police registered a second FIR after detecting five allegedly forged Police Verification Certificates (PVCs) created in the names of different applicants and purportedly passed off as genuine documents issued by the police department.
The case was registered on November 17 based on a complaint filed by Nagaraj T. Nedalagi, Police Inspector attached to the City Special Branch, Bengaluru.
According to the complaint, the Inspector received information on November 17 about the creation of fake police verification certificates. A preliminary examination revealed that five certificates issued in the names of different applicants were not genuine documents authorised by the Bengaluru City Police.
The certificates allegedly carried the following applicants’ names and reference numbers: Himanshu Nayak, Dushasan Swain, Ravikumar, Rathul Mili and Dibyanranjan Beura. Police suspect that the accused created the forged certificates and attempted to use them as genuine documents before various departments and authorities to commit fraud and secure undue benefits.
The complaint has sought an investigation to identify those involved in creating the certificates, those who assisted in their preparation and those who used them. Police will also investigate the purpose behind creating the documents, the method adopted and the departments or authorities before which they were submitted.

briefs.headline: Groundnut shortfall forces Malleswaram’s Kadlekai Parishe to look beyond Karnataka
briefs.deck: Farmers from Hosur and other parts of Tamil Nadu, along with those from Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, will participate in the three-day fair, bringing their produce for sale
briefs.bodyText:
With groundnut production in Karnataka expected to decline due to drought conditions this year, the 10th annual Kadlekai Parishe in Malleswaram will depend on supplies from neighbouring States, including Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, to meet the demand for groundnuts.
Farmers from Hosur and other parts of Tamil Nadu, along with those from Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, will participate in the three-day fair, bringing their produce for sale. Organised by the Kadu Malleshwara Geleyara Balaga, the fair will be held from November 28 to 30 along Kadumalleshwara Temple Road and Sampige Road in Malleswaram, Bengaluru.
B.K. Shivaram, president of the Kadu Malleshwara Geleyara Balaga, said, “Groundnut production across Karnataka may have declined due to drought conditions this year. Farmers from Magadi, Bengaluru Rural, Kolar and Chitradurga will participate in the fair. However, a majority of the participating farmers are from Hosur and other parts of Tamil Nadu. A few farmers from Andhra Pradesh and Telangana will also bring their produce for sale.”
Despite the challenging conditions, the organisers aim to encourage farmers by providing them with direct market access. “Around 600 stalls will be set up, and no rental fee will be collected from farmers and traders,” Mr. Shivaram added.
The parishe will be inaugurated on November 28 by Minister for Muzrai and Fisheries, Ports and Inland Water Transport K.S. Basavanthappa, Minister of Forest, Ecology and Environment Ramalinga Reddy, and Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee president B.K. Hariprasad.
Plastic-free
The organisers have planned several initiatives to make this year’s parishe plastic-free. Free cloth and paper bags will be distributed to farmers, stall owners and visitors to discourage the use of plastic. Any plastic bags found during the fair will be collected and disposed of, Mr. Shivaram said.
Another attraction will be handmade gifts prepared by children using bamboo grown on the temple premises. These gifts will be presented to distinguished guests. Bamboo will also be used to construct the stage for the event.
Award
The Hunnime Haadu 2026 Rajyotsava Annual Award will be presented to Vanaja P. Poornarthi Bitpadi from Udupi in recognition of her humanitarian service. She has been performing the last rites and arranging dignified funerals for unclaimed and abandoned bodies.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru: East corporation’s mobile veterinary service treats 487 cases in five months
briefs.deck: The mobile ambulance service was launched to provide timely treatment and medical assistance to animals suffering from illnesses, injuries, and other health complications within the corporation’s limits.
briefs.bodyText:
As many as 487 cases involving community animals have been treated by the Bengaluru East City Corporation’s mobile veterinary service in the five months, according to the corporation. The novel initiative was launched in July this year.
The mobile ambulance service was launched to provide timely treatment and medical assistance to animals suffering from illnesses, injuries, and other health complications within the corporation’s limits. It primarily caters to injured, sick, and critically ill community animals requiring urgent veterinary care.
D.S. Ramesh, commissioner of East City Corporation, said the service was receiving an encouraging response from the public and was playing a significant role in providing veterinary assistance to community animals.
The mobile veterinary unit treated 155 cases in October, the highest in a month so far. This was followed by 133 cases in September, 95 in August, and 95 in November up to November 22. About nine cases were treated in July, according to the monthly reports.
The services include treatment for common ailments, wounds, bites and injuries caused by accidents, skin infections, digestive and respiratory disorders, and conditions affecting various other systems of the body. The unit also provides vaccination and emergency ambulance services, including transportation of animals.
The corporation said the mobile veterinary unit helps community animals access free medical care and extends veterinary assistance to areas where access to such facilities is limited or difficult.

stories.headline: Global climate talks must shut door on fossil fuel ‘clout’
stories.deck: The breakdown in the Antalya summit has deepened the crisis of confidence in climate diplomacy, making transparency and accountability in the negotiating process more urgent than ever.
stories.bodyText:
The failure of the United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, to agree on its central political statement, with countries unable to bridge their differences over fossil fuels and other key questions of climate action, has exposed the fragility of international climate cooperation. It should also sharpen scrutiny of who gets access to climate negotiations, whose interests they represent and what safeguards keep decisions accountable to the public.
The Türkiye summit ended without agreement on an overarching statement. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said he shared the “deep disappointment” of many that the conference was unable to reach consensus on a statement that typically sends a policy signal to all nations. Some separate negotiating decisions were reached though. Nevertheless, the absence of a political consensus was a serious setback.
The breakdown does not show that fossil fuel lobbying caused the impasse. But it does make more urgent a separate question about the credibility of the process. A forum that asks governments to make decisions in the global public interest must be transparent about who is seeking to shape those decisions, what interests they represent and how conflicts are managed.
The international climate negotiations that take place every year still lack a comprehensive, enforceable system to identify and manage conflicts of interest involving powerful commercial interests, including fossil fuel companies and state-owned energy businesses. The Antalya conference has underlined why that gap matters.

stories.headline: Rs 2.73 cr rent taxed as business income, taxable income hits Rs 1.07 cr; ITAT rules for landlord
stories.deck: A landlord earned Rs 2.73 crore in rent from his commercial properties and reported the amount in his income tax return (ITR) under the “Income from House Property” head. However, the AO reclassified the rental receipts as business income. This pushed the landlord’s total taxable income up from the Rs 24.07 lakh that he had originally declared to Rs 1.07 crore.
stories.bodyText:
You earn rental income from commercial properties. When filing your income tax return, under what head can you classify it?
In one case, a landlord earned rent from and reported the amount in his income tax return (ITR) under the “Income from House Property” head. However, the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) issued him a notice and classified the rental receipts as business income.
What the case is about
A landlord earned Rs 2.73 crore in rent from his commercial properties and reported the amount in his income tax return (ITR) under the “Income from House Property” head.
However, the AO reclassified the rental receipts as business income. This pushed the landlord’s total taxable income up from the Rs 24.07 lakh that he had originally declared to Rs 1.07 crore.
The sharp increase resulted from the change in the tax treatment of his rental earnings. Under the “Income from House Property” head, taxpayers can claim a flat standard deduction of 30% on the net annual value after deducting eligible municipal taxes paid.
When rental receipts are assessed as business income, however, taxpayers can claim eligible business expenses incurred to earn that income. This difference in the deductions available explains why the landlord’s taxable income rose from Rs 24.07 lakh to Rs 1.07 crore.
The landlord calculated that if his rental earnings of around Rs 2.7 crore were assessed as income from house property, he would be entitled to claim Rs 81.52 lakh as a standard deduction under Section 24, along with Rs 1.63 lakh for municipal taxes he had paid, according to an ET report on the judgement.
By treating the rent as business income, the AO denied the landlord the benefit of the deductions available under the house-property head. The CIT (Appeals) subsequently upheld the AO’s decision.
The landlord then challenged the order before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Surat. On November 4, 2026, he won on the key question of how his rental income should be classified for tax purposes.
Why did ITAT Surat give relief to landlord?
The landlord’s business involves dealing in land and constructing buildings. He earned rent from industrial buildings that formed part of his stock-in-trade, or business assets. The Assessing Officer relied on this aspect while assessing the rental receipts under the head “Income from Business or Profession”.
The landlord, however, maintained that his business was the “business of dealing in lands and construction of buildings”, and not the “business of letting out buildings”.
ITAT Surat held that the fact that he dealt in land, constructed buildings and rented out properties held as stock-in-trade for sale did not, by itself, settle the question of how the rental receipts should be classified. The determining factor was the nature of the activity from which the income arose.
The tribunal referred to the Supreme Court’s ruling in Chennai Properties and Investments Ltd. (supra), in which rental income was treated as business income because letting out properties was itself the assessee’s business.
However, ITAT Surat distinguished that ruling, along with the other judgments relied upon by the CIT (Appeals), on the ground that those cases involved taxpayers whose business was letting out properties.
The tribunal also noted that the Gujarat High Court’s ruling in Commissioner of Income-tax v. New India Industries Ltd. (1993) 201 ITR 208 (Guj) supported the landlord’s contention that his rental earnings were taxable under the head “Income from House Property”.
The tribunal further observed that the lower authorities had not recorded any finding that the landlord was engaged in the business of letting out properties. It also noted that no material had been placed before it to establish that he was carrying on such a business.
Chartered Accountant Chintan Ghelani told ET that the landlord’s case succeeded because ITAT Surat distinguished between conducting a real-estate business and carrying on a business of letting out properties.
Ghelani explained that rent earned from industrial buildings cannot automatically be classified as business income merely because those properties are held as stock-in-trade, or business assets.
Under income tax law, rental earnings from letting out properties, including buildings, are ordinarily taxable as house-property income under Section 22. However, such receipts may be assessed as business income if the facts establish that letting out properties is itself the taxpayer’s business.
In this case, ITAT Surat observed that the lower authorities had not recorded any finding that he was engaged in the business of letting out properties. Nor had any material been brought before the tribunal to establish that this was the nature of his business.
Ghelani also pointed out that Section 23(5) expressly recognises that a property forming part of stock-in-trade can still come within the scope of the house-property provisions. Therefore, while the classification of a property as stock-in-trade is relevant, it does not, by itself, determine the tax head under which its rental income must be assessed.
In its order, ITAT Surat ruled in favour of the landlord on the classification of his rental income, holding that the Rs 2.73 crore received from industrial buildings held as stock-in-trade was taxable under the head “Income from House Property” and not “Income from Business or Profession”.
The tribunal directed the Assessing Officer to recompute his income under the house-property head, allow deductions admissible under the Income Tax Act and grant consequential relief in accordance with the law.
It also directed the AO to ensure that expenses were not deducted twice under different heads of income.

British drugmaker GSK’s subsidiary GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals (GSK India), as part of a strategy to sharpen focus on cancer therapies, on Tuesday announced the launch of monoclonal antibody-drug conjugate BLENREP (belantamab mafodotin) as a combination therapy for those with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma.

briefs.headline: Nasdaq retreats after Nvidia-fuelled rally; Anthropic slips below IPO price
briefs.bodyText:
Wall Street retreated on Tuesday as technology stocks gave back some of the previous day's sharp gains, with investors booking profits and turning cautious ahead of key US inflation data. Nvidia and Anthropic led the decline in AI-linked stocks.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48% to 23,733.54, while the S&P 500 declined 0.50% to 7,201.09. However, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 423.39 points, or 0.85%, to 50,018.70.
The pullback came a day after Wall Street staged a strong rally, driven by Nvidia's decision to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO. The rebound, however, failed to ease concerns over stretched AI valuations, rising infrastructure spending and the outlook for interest rates.
Anthropic falls below IPO price
Anthropic shares tumbled 6.5% to $81.90, slipping below their initial public offering (IPO) price of $83, just days after the AI startup's record-breaking Nasdaq debut.
The stock opened at $111.50 on November 19, with its fully diluted valuation briefly exceeding $2 trillion. However, it has since lost ground amid a broader technology selloff.
Anthropic raised $93.5 billion in its IPO after underwriters exercised their option to purchase additional shares, making it the biggest public offering on record and surpassing SpaceX's $85.7 billion listing in June.
CEO Dario Amodei sold more than 3.37 million shares worth over $280 million a day after the IPO, according to a filing late on Monday.
The company's rapid reversal has renewed concerns about elevated AI valuations and the massive investments being made in computing infrastructure, particularly as higher interest rates could increase financing costs, Reuters reported.
Anthropic is not the first major technology company to fall below its IPO price soon after listing. SpaceX took about a month to slip below its offer price, while Facebook, now Meta Platforms, fell below its IPO price on its second trading day in 2012.
Nvidia, chip stocks retreat after rally
Nvidia shares fell 5.9% as investors reassessed the implications of Jensen Huang's return as CEO and the political and governance risks surrounding the company.
The chipmaker had surged nearly 30% on Monday after Huang's reinstatement, helping the S&P 500 and Nasdaq post their biggest daily percentage gains since April 2025.
Technology stocks led the declines on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 technology sector falling 2.8%. The semiconductor index dropped 7.9%, reflecting renewed selling in AI-linked companies.
Before Monday's rally, AI stocks had struggled for weeks as investors questioned whether the sector's debt-fuelled spending on infrastructure would generate sufficient returns.
Investors await US inflation data, tariff developments
Investors are also looking ahead to Wednesday's Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, a key inflation gauge watched by the Federal Reserve ahead of its December policy meeting.
Persistent inflation has strengthened expectations of tighter monetary policy. Fed funds futures traders were pricing in a 98% probability of a rate hike in December and a 66% chance of another increase in January, according to CME Group's FedWatch Tool.
New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said late on Monday that persistently high inflation continues to point towards tighter monetary policy.
Investors were also wary of potential new tariffs after Reuters reported, citing three people familiar with the matter, that the Trump administration was preparing to release findings of a probe into alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 major US trading partners. The findings are expected to pave the way for new import duties on a wide range of goods.
The administration's tariffs have contributed to higher consumer prices in the US, adding to inflation concerns.
Dollar slips, bond yields steady
The dollar fell 0.44% against a basket of major currencies, retreating from a 20-month high touched earlier in the session.
The yield on benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes edged up 0.77 basis points to 4.928%, compared with 4.92% late on Monday.
The gap between two-year and 10-year Treasury yields, a closely watched indicator of economic expectations, stood at 24.3 basis points.
Gold futures fell 2.67% and silver futures dropped 5.75%, pressured by hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials and expectations of higher interest rates.
Brent crude futures settled $2.03 higher, or 2.27%, at $91.40 a barrel after a volatile session, with fresh attacks reported on vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz.

briefs.headline: RBI to widen market for government securities: DG Jain
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: 
RBI
 is seeking to broaden retail participation in govt securities (G-secs) and improve secondary-market liquidity by making it easier for individual investors to access the market and encouraging primary dealers (PDs) to expand their market-making activities.
Speaking at Primary Dealers’ Association of India (PDAI) Seminar 2026 here on Monday, RBI deputy governor Rohit Jain outlined measures to widen the investor base and distribute trading activity more evenly across the yield curve at a time when there is a drop in demand from long-term institutional investors.
“It has been observed that demand from banks, insurers and pension funds for long-term sovereign debt has marginally declined, with insurance and pension funds shifting towards more of equity exposure. This has structurally reduced such demand for govt securities,” said Jain.
To widen the investor base, Jain said PDs could play a greater role by acting as active market makers under the scheme, conducting awareness campaigns and educating retail investors about the benefits of these instruments. They could also tailor bond offerings to retail investors, including shorter-tenor STRIPS (Separate Trading of Registered Interest and Principal of Securities), which are relatively easier to understand.
To improve secondary-market liquidity, RBI has reduced the frequency of benchmark G-sec issuances and increased the volume offered in each auction. These measures have helped improve trading liquidity, but it remains lower than in other countries.
Jain said PDs should increase market-making activity, particularly by providing two-way quotes in off-the-run securities.
